cur:monumental-santa-prassede-zeno-vault.summary: At the crown of the gold-covered vault, a bust of Christ in a blue medallion is held aloft by four white-robed angels who stand in the corners with arms raised, like caryatids of heaven. The whole small chapel seems to rise towards this image, so that those praying beneath stand under the gaze of Christ.
facts: The Chapel of Saint Zeno was built by Pope Paschal I (817–824) as a funerary chapel for his mother, Theodora; its walls and vault are almost entirely clad in gold-ground mosaic.
The four angels holding a medallion of Christ adapt an imperial and Ravennate motif, also found in the Archiepiscopal Chapel and San Vitale in Ravenna.
Paschal I's mosaics belong to the Carolingian-era revival in Rome, when the pope also translated many martyrs' relics from the catacombs into the city's churches.
